- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 70–72 range); add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for 3–5 periods post-reversion.  
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts; apply 1–3 day delay correction for sentiment-driven moves.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1.4, -1.0, +1.4), model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
